title: Ezekiel Chapter 26 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 26 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 26 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 26.

questions.question: On which day and year did the word of the LORD come to Ezekiel in this chapter?
options: Eleventh year, first day of the month
Tenth year, fifth day of the month
Twelfth year, tenth day of the month
Eleventh year, fifteenth day of the month
questions.correctAnswer: Eleventh year, first day of the month
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:1 states the word of the LORD came to Ezekiel in the eleventh year, in the first day of the month.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 26, what city had spoken against Jerusalem saying, 'Aha, she is broken'?
options: Tyrus
Babylon
Nineveh
Jericho
questions.correctAnswer: Tyrus
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:2 explicitly mentions Tyrus as the city that said against Jerusalem, 'Aha, she is broken.'

questions.question: What reason did Tyrus give for expecting to be replenished?
options: Because Jerusalem is laid waste
Because Babylon will help them
Because their walls are strong
Because their ships are many
questions.correctAnswer: Because Jerusalem is laid waste
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:2 says Tyrus said, 'I shall be replenished, now she is laid waste,' referring to Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does the Lord GOD say He will cause to come against Tyrus?
options: Many nations
A great flood
A famine
Locusts
questions.correctAnswer: Many nations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:3 records the Lord GOD saying He will cause many nations to come up against Tyrus.

questions.question: What will happen to the walls and towers of Tyrus according to the prophecy?
options: They shall be destroyed and broken down
They shall be strengthened
They shall be ignored
They shall be painted
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be destroyed and broken down
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:4 promises the walls and towers of Tyrus will be destroyed and broken down.

questions.question: What will Tyrus become after it is destroyed?
options: A place for spreading nets in the sea
A flourishing city
A land of vineyards
A mountain of gold
questions.correctAnswer: A place for spreading nets in the sea
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:5 states that Tyrus will become a place for the spreading of nets in the midst of the sea.

questions.question: What will happen to the 'daughters' of Tyrus in the field?
options: They shall be slain by the sword
They shall be taken captive
They shall be hidden
They shall be spared
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be slain by the sword
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:6 says her daughters in the field shall be slain by the sword.

questions.question: Who is the king that the Lord GOD says He will bring upon Tyrus?
options: Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon
Cyrus king of Persia
Pharaoh king of Egypt
Alexander king of Macedonia
questions.correctAnswer: Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:7 identifies Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon as the one the Lord GOD will bring upon Tyrus.

questions.question: From what direction will Nebuchadrezzar come against Tyrus?
options: From the north
From the south
From the east
From the west
questions.correctAnswer: From the north
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:7 mentions Nebuchadrezzar coming from the north with horses and chariots.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord GOD said He would make Tyrus like the top of a rock.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:4 states that the Lord GOD would make Tyrus like the top of a rock.

questions.question: True or False: Nebuchadrezzar will come to Tyrus with only a few soldiers.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:7 says Nebuchadrezzar will come with horses, chariots, horsemen, companies, and much people, not just a few soldiers.

questions.question: True or False: The daughters of Tyrus mentioned in Ezekiel 26:6 refer to other cities allied with Tyrus in the field.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:6 refers to daughters in the field being slain, indicating allied cities or territories related to Tyrus.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 26:3 compares the nations coming against Tyrus to the waves of the sea.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:3 says many nations will come against Tyrus as the sea causes its waves to come up.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 26, which event comes first?
options: The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel
Nebuchadrezzar attacks Tyrus
The walls of Tyrus are destroyed
The daughters of Tyrus are slain
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:1 shows the word of the LORD coming to Ezekiel first, before the other events.

questions.question: What is the intended result when the walls and towers of Tyrus are destroyed?
options: Tyrus shall be scraped to dust and made like the top of a rock
Tyrus shall become a kingdom of many nations
Tyrus shall be rebuilt and strengthened
Tyrus shall become a city of refuge
questions.correctAnswer: Tyrus shall be scraped to dust and made like the top of a rock
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:4 states the Lord GOD will scrape her dust and make her like the top of a rock after destruction.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 26 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 26 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 26:8, what military actions will Nebuchadrezzar take against Tyrus?
options: He will make a fort, cast a mount, and lift up a buckler against Tyrus
He will negotiate peace and establish trade agreements
He will send envoys to Tyrus to demand tribute
He will ignore Tyrus and attack other cities
questions.correctAnswer: He will make a fort, cast a mount, and lift up a buckler against Tyrus
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:8 clearly states that Nebuchadrezzar will make a fort against Tyrus, cast a mount, and lift up the buckler against it, indicating a full military siege. This is supported by the surrounding verses 7 and 9, which describe the king of Babylon coming with much people and setting engines of war.

questions.question: What method will be used to break down the towers of Tyrus as described in Ezekiel 26:9?
options: With axes by the king of Babylon
By fire set by the inhabitants
By a great flood
Through peaceful surrender
questions.correctAnswer: With axes by the king of Babylon
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:9 specifies that the king of Babylon will set engines of war against the walls and break down the towers with axes, showing a violent siege. This aligns with verse 8's description of the military actions and verse 10's depiction of the noise and dust of horses accompanying the attack.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 26:10 describe the effect of the abundance of horses on the city of Tyrus?
options: The dust of their horses will cover Tyrus and the walls will shake
The horses will flee in fear from the city
The horses will be used to build new walls
The city will welcome the horses peacefully
questions.correctAnswer: The dust of their horses will cover Tyrus and the walls will shake
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:10 explains that the abundance of horses will cause dust to cover Tyrus and make the walls shake at the noise of horsemen, wheels, and chariots, illustrating the overwhelming nature of the siege. This complements the siege preparation in verses 8 and 9.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 26:11, what will happen to the streets and people of Tyrus during the attack?
options: The horses will tread down the streets and the people will be slain by the sword
The streets will be preserved and no harm will come to the people
The people will flee before the horses arrive
The streets will be flooded to stop the horses
questions.correctAnswer: The horses will tread down the streets and the people will be slain by the sword
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:11 states that the horses' hoofs will tread down all the streets and the people will be slain by the sword, with strong garrisons falling, indicating total destruction. This continues the depiction of violent conquest seen in verses 8 through 10.

questions.question: What will happen to the riches and merchandise of Tyrus according to Ezekiel 26:12?
options: They will be spoiled and preyed upon by the attackers
They will be hidden and preserved by the inhabitants
They will be sent as tribute to Jerusalem
They will be destroyed by fire without being taken
questions.correctAnswer: They will be spoiled and preyed upon by the attackers
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:12 describes how the riches and merchandise of Tyrus will be made spoil and prey by the attackers, who will also break down walls and destroy houses. This complements the destruction detailed in verses 8 to 11.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 26:13 say will happen to the noise of songs and the sound of harps in Tyrus?
options: They will cease and be no more heard
They will increase in celebration of victory
They will be heard throughout the land
They will be replaced by the sound of bells
questions.correctAnswer: They will cease and be no more heard
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:13 clearly states that the noise of songs will cease and the sound of harps will no longer be heard, symbolizing the end of joy and celebration in Tyrus after its destruction, fitting the theme of judgment in verses 8–12.

questions.question: What ultimate transformation does God declare He will bring upon Tyrus in Ezekiel 26:14?
options: It will become like the top of a rock and a place to spread nets
It will be rebuilt into a great city
It will become a mountain of gold
It will be submerged permanently under sand
questions.correctAnswer: It will become like the top of a rock and a place to spread nets
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:14 states that Tyrus will be made like the top of a rock and a place to spread nets upon, and it shall not be rebuilt, emphasizing permanent desolation as decreed by the Lord, consistent with the destruction described in the preceding verses.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 26:9 imply about the nature of the siege engines used against Tyrus?
options: They were powerful and capable of breaking down towers
They were ineffective and easily destroyed
They were symbolic and not actually used
They were used to defend the city walls
questions.correctAnswer: They were powerful and capable of breaking down towers
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:9 indicates that engines of war were set against Tyrus’s walls and with axes they broke down the towers, signifying the siege engines' destructive power, which aligns with the aggressive siege tactics in verses 8 and 10.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 26:10 describes the walls of Tyrus shaking due to the noise of horsemen and chariots during the siege.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:10 explicitly mentions that the walls shall shake at the noise of horsemen, wheels, and chariots entering the city, confirming the intense pressure of the siege.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 26:14 teach about God's authority over the future of cities like Tyrus?
options: God declares Tyrus will not be rebuilt, showing His sovereign judgment
God promises to restore Tyrus to its former glory
God leaves the fate of Tyrus to human rulers
God will protect Tyrus from all enemies
questions.correctAnswer: God declares Tyrus will not be rebuilt, showing His sovereign judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:14 states God will make Tyrus like the top of a rock and it shall be built no more, demonstrating God’s sovereign power to decree the destiny of nations and cities, consistent with His judgments in verses 8 to 13.

questions.question: Based on Ezekiel 26:11-12, what practical lesson about trusting worldly riches can a believer learn?
options: Worldly riches can be taken away suddenly and should not be our ultimate security
Accumulating riches guarantees protection from harm
Riches will always be preserved by divine intervention
Riches are a sign of God’s unending blessing
questions.correctAnswer: Worldly riches can be taken away suddenly and should not be our ultimate security
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:11-12 describes how the riches and merchandise of Tyrus will be plundered and destroyed, teaching believers that trust in material wealth is insecure, aligning with biblical principles of faith and humility in God rather than possessions.

questions.question: Context question: What does Ezekiel 26:13 promise will happen if the attackers break down the walls and destroy the houses as described in Ezekiel 26:12?
options: The noise of songs and harps will cease in Tyrus
The city will immediately be rebuilt
The people will celebrate their victory
The city will become a trading hub again
questions.correctAnswer: The noise of songs and harps will cease in Tyrus
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:12 describes the destruction of walls and houses, and verse 13 promises that as a result, the joyful noise of songs and harps will cease, showing the total end of Tyrus’s prosperity and celebration, linking the cause and effect between these verses.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 26:8-14 teach us about the consequences of pride and opposition to God’s people?
options: Pride and opposition lead to downfall and destruction as seen with Tyrus
Pride leads to immediate success and dominance
Opposition to God’s people is ignored by God
Pride results in increased wealth and security
questions.correctAnswer: Pride and opposition lead to downfall and destruction as seen with Tyrus
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:2-3 shows Tyrus boasting against Jerusalem, and verses 8-14 describe God’s judgment through destruction, teaching believers that prideful opposition to God’s people results in God’s decisive judgment and downfall.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 26:14 assures that Tyrus will be rebuilt and flourish again after the siege.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:14 explicitly states that Tyrus shall be built no more, confirming permanent destruction rather than restoration.

questions.question: What attitude will the princes of the sea have toward Tyrus’s fall, according to Ezekiel 26:16?
options: They will tremble, put off their robes, and sit in astonishment
They will rejoice and celebrate loudly
They will ignore the fall and continue ruling
They will attack their own cities in fear
questions.correctAnswer: They will tremble, put off their robes, and sit in astonishment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:16 describes the princes of the sea laying away their robes and trembling in astonishment at Tyrus’s fall, showing the widespread impact and fear caused by this judgment, consistent with the theme of total destruction.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 26 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 26.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 26, what will be the reaction of the 'princes of the sea' upon the fall of Tyrus?
options: They will rejoice and celebrate
They shall come down from their thrones, lay away their robes, clothe themselves with trembling, and be astonished
They will ignore the event
They will wage war against Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: They shall come down from their thrones, lay away their robes, clothe themselves with trembling, and be astonished
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:16 states that the princes of the sea will come down from their thrones, lay away their robes and broidered garments, clothe themselves with trembling, sit upon the ground, and be astonished at Tyrus.

questions.question: What is the significance of Tyrus being made 'like the top of a rock' according to Ezekiel 26?
options: It will be a place to spread nets upon, never to be rebuilt
It will be a new kingdom's capital
It will become a mountain of gold
It will be a sanctuary for refugees
questions.correctAnswer: It will be a place to spread nets upon, never to be rebuilt
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:14 explains that Tyrus will be made like the top of a rock, a place to spread nets upon, and it shall be built no more, indicating complete desolation.

questions.question: Which Babylonian king is prophesied to bring destruction upon Tyrus?
options: Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon
Cyrus king of Persia
Darius king of Persia
Nebuchadnezzar king of Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:7 identifies Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon as the one who will come from the north to bring destruction upon Tyrus.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 26:21, what will happen to Tyrus after its destruction?
options: It will be rebuilt and prosper
It will be a terror and never be found again
It will become a trading hub
It will be inhabited by new peoples
questions.correctAnswer: It will be a terror and never be found again
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:21 states that Tyrus will become a terror, be no more, and though sought for, it shall never be found again.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 26:19 mean by bringing 'up the deep upon thee' and 'great waters shall cover thee'?
options: A literal flood will cover the city
The city will be submerged or destroyed by the sea
The city will receive abundant rain
The city will be blessed with water
questions.correctAnswer: The city will be submerged or destroyed by the sea
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:19 uses imagery of the deep and great waters covering Tyrus, symbolizing desolation and submersion, consistent with its coastal location.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 26 prophesies that Tyrus' daughters in the field will be spared during the coming destruction.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:6 clearly states that her daughters in the field shall be slain by the sword, showing no sparing of them.

questions.question: What literary device is predominantly used in Ezekiel 26:15-18 when describing the reaction of the isles and princes at Tyrus' fall?
options: Chiasm
Parallelism
Metaphor
Simile
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:15-18 uses parallelism, evidenced by repeated phrases and mirrored ideas about the trembling and lamentation of the isles and princes, a common Hebrew poetic device.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage shares a thematic connection with Ezekiel 26's prophecy of Tyrus' destruction as a judgment of God against pride and wealth?
options: Isaiah 23
Genesis 1
Psalms 23
Exodus 20
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 23
questions.explanation: Isaiah 23 also prophesies the fall of Tyrus, connecting with Ezekiel 26's theme of divine judgment against a proud and wealthy maritime city.

questions.question: What Hebrew word meaning 'to spread' or 'to stretch' is significant in Ezekiel 26:5 and 26:14 concerning Tyrus, and what does it symbolize?
options: Nets (Hebrew: 'reshet') symbolizing fishing and desolation
Chariot (Hebrew: 'merkavah') symbolizing war
Rock (Hebrew: 'tsur') symbolizing strength
Dust (Hebrew: 'aphar') symbolizing destruction
questions.correctAnswer: Nets (Hebrew: 'reshet') symbolizing fishing and desolation
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'reshet' (nets) is used in Ezekiel 26:5 and 26:14 to describe Tyrus becoming a place to spread nets, symbolizing its ruin and conversion into a fishing spot rather than a thriving city.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 26:20 relate the fate of Tyrus to 'them that descend into the pit' and what is the theological implication?
options: Tyrus will join the dead in Sheol, signifying total destruction and loss of status
Tyrus will be resurrected
Tyrus will become a heavenly city
Tyrus will be forgotten like a dream
questions.correctAnswer: Tyrus will join the dead in Sheol, signifying total destruction and loss of status
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:20 references 'them that descend into the pit,' an Old Testament term for the dead or Sheol, indicating that Tyrus will be utterly destroyed and consigned to oblivion.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of judgment against a proud and wealthy city similar to Ezekiel 26's prophecy against Tyrus?
options: Revelation 18
Matthew 5
John 3
Acts 2
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 18
questions.explanation: Revelation 18 describes the fall of Babylon the great, a wealthy and proud city, echoing Ezekiel 26's theme of divine judgment against Tyrus.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 26:13 mean by 'I will cause the noise of thy songs to cease; and the sound of thy harps shall be no more heard' in relation to Tyrus?
options: It symbolizes the end of Tyrus' cultural and joyful life
It means Tyrus will stop making music temporarily
It implies Tyrus will convert to another religion
It means Tyrus will become mute
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the end of Tyrus' cultural and joyful life
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:13 uses the cessation of songs and harp music as a metaphor for the complete devastation and end of Tyrus' prosperity and joy.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 26, the destruction of Tyrus will cause the surrounding islands to tremble and be troubled.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:18 explicitly states that the isles shall tremble and be troubled at the departure of Tyrus, indicating the wide impact of its fall.

questions.question: What is the role of Nebuchadrezzar's 'engines of war' and 'axes' as described in Ezekiel 26:9?
options: They are literal weapons used to break down walls and towers of Tyrus
They are symbolic words for spiritual warfare
They are diplomatic tools
They are musical instruments
questions.correctAnswer: They are literal weapons used to break down walls and towers of Tyrus
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:9 describes Nebuchadrezzar setting engines of war against Tyrus' walls and breaking down towers with axes, indicating physical siege warfare.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 26:15 use the imagery of 'the isles shaking at the sound of thy fall' to emphasize the impact of Tyrus' destruction?
options: It emphasizes the widespread shock and fear caused by Tyrus' downfall among maritime nations
It indicates an earthquake literally shaking the isles
It suggests the isles will send armies to rescue Tyrus
It refers to a musical event
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the widespread shock and fear caused by Tyrus' downfall among maritime nations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:15 uses the isles shaking as a metaphor for the terror and astonishment among surrounding nations at Tyrus' destruction.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 26 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 26 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily demonstrated by God's declaration against Tyre in Ezekiel 26:3?
options: God's omnipotence in executing judgment
God's mercy to sinners
God's patience toward the nations
God's grace to the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotence in executing judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:3 shows God's sovereign power to raise many nations against Tyre, like waves of the sea, demonstrating His omnipotence in orchestrating judgment.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 26:4, what final state will God bring upon Tyre?
options: It will become a desolate rock
It will be rebuilt and prosper
It will turn into a fertile land
It will become a place of refuge
questions.correctAnswer: It will become a desolate rock
questions.explanation: Verse 4 declares that God will scrape Tyre’s dust and make it like the top of a rock, symbolizing utter desolation and removal of its former glory.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God's judgment is revealed by the description in Ezekiel 26:6?
options: Judgment serves to reveal God's sovereignty
Judgment is arbitrary and unpredictable
Judgment is limited to the wicked only
Judgment excludes the innocent
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment serves to reveal God's sovereignty
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:6 says the daughters in the field shall be slain and they shall know that God is the LORD, showing that judgment reveals God's sovereign authority.

questions.question: Who does God raise up as the instrument of judgment against Tyre in Ezekiel 26:7?
options: Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon
Cyrus king of Persia
Alexander the Great
King David
questions.correctAnswer: Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 26:7 explicitly names Nebuchadrezzar, king of Babylon, as the king of kings from the north who will bring judgment upon Tyre.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 26:8 reveal about the military strategy used against Tyre?
options: A fort and mount were raised against the city
A siege by famine only
Attack through naval blockade
Negotiations without warfare
questions.correctAnswer: A fort and mount were raised against the city
questions.explanation: Verse 8 states that Nebuchadrezzar will build a fort, cast up a mount, and lift a shield against Tyre, describing a direct military siege strategy.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 26:12 portray the extent of destruction upon Tyre?
options: Walls and houses destroyed, materials thrown into the sea
City preserved but weakened
Only the walls breached
The city surrendered peacefully
questions.correctAnswer: Walls and houses destroyed, materials thrown into the sea
questions.explanation: Verse 12 describes how the walls, pleasant houses, stones, timber, and dust will be broken down and cast into the water, indicating total ruin.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed by the cessation of Tyre’s songs and harps in Ezekiel 26:13?
options: God’s justice in silencing false pride
God’s grace to restore joy
God’s long-suffering patience
God’s mercy in discipline
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice in silencing false pride
questions.explanation: The cessation of songs and harps in verse 13 symbolizes God's justice in silencing Tyre’s pride and joy as a consequence of judgment.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by comparing Ezekiel 26:5 and 26:14 about Tyre’s fate?
options: Tyre will become a fishing place and never rebuilt
Tyre will be a place of blessing for the nations
Tyre will be restored to its former glory
Tyre will be a symbol of peace
questions.correctAnswer: Tyre will become a fishing place and never rebuilt
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 14 together state Tyre will be made like the top of a rock, a place to spread nets, and it shall not be rebuilt, showing permanent desolation.

questions.question: How do Ezekiel 26:15 and 26:16 contribute to understanding the impact of Tyre’s fall in the ancient world?
options: The surrounding islands and princes will tremble and mourn
Tyre’s fall will go unnoticed
It will bring immediate peace to the region
Other cities will rejoice at Tyre’s destruction
questions.correctAnswer: The surrounding islands and princes will tremble and mourn
questions.explanation: Verses 15 and 16 depict the shaking of the isles and the princes of the sea laying aside their robes, trembling and mourning, showing Tyre’s significant regional influence.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 26:19 teach about God’s sovereign control over nature in judgment?
options: God can bring deep waters upon a city to desolate it
God leaves natural disasters to chance
God’s judgment never involves nature
God protects cities from floods
questions.correctAnswer: God can bring deep waters upon a city to desolate it
questions.explanation: Verse 19 states God will bring up the deep and cover Tyre with great waters, showing divine sovereignty over natural elements in executing judgment.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 26:20, what is the ultimate fate of Tyre in relation to the dead and the living?
options: Tyre will be set among the dead and not inhabited among the living
Tyre will be exalted among the nations
Tyre will be a place of refuge for the living
Tyre will become a center of worship
questions.correctAnswer: Tyre will be set among the dead and not inhabited among the living
questions.explanation: Verse 20 explains God will bring Tyre down to the low parts of the earth with the people of old, making it uninhabited, contrasting the land of the living with desolation.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do Ezekiel 26:11 and 26:12 convey about God’s judgment on sin and material wealth?
options: God’s judgment destroys both people and their riches
God preserves material wealth despite judgment
God rewards the sinful with riches
God’s judgment spares the innocent and their property
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment destroys both people and their riches
questions.explanation: Verses 11 and 12 describe slaughter of people and spoil of riches, showing God’s comprehensive judgment on both human life and material wealth associated with sin.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 26:21 reveal about God’s ultimate purpose in making Tyre a terror and no more?
options: To demonstrate that the wicked cannot escape divine judgment
To elevate Tyre as a warning for righteousness
To show favoritism for Tyre
To protect Tyre from destruction
questions.correctAnswer: To demonstrate that the wicked cannot escape divine judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 21 declares Tyre will be made a terror and never found again despite being sought, illustrating that God’s judgment is final and inescapable for the wicked.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s judgment against Tyre was merely political and not divinely ordained. What does Ezekiel 26:7-10 actually teach about the nature of this judgment?
options: God sovereignly raises Nebuchadrezzar as His instrument to execute judgment
The judgment was a random military conquest without divine purpose
Tyre fell due to internal political strife alone
The text does not mention any divine involvement
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly raises Nebuchadrezzar as His instrument to execute judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 7-10 emphasize that God declares He will bring Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon to execute judgment, showing divine sovereignty over political events.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 26:2 reveal the sin of Tyre in relation to Jerusalem and God’s holy city?
options: Tyre rejoiced over Jerusalem’s destruction, showing pride and arrogance
Tyre mourned with Jerusalem over its troubles
Tyre remained neutral regarding Jerusalem
Tyre sought peace with Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Tyre rejoiced over Jerusalem’s destruction, showing pride and arrogance
questions.explanation: Verse 2 records Tyre saying 'Aha' over Jerusalem’s broken gates and waste, revealing sinful pride and rejoicing in another’s judgment.
